answers.answer: The first Fear completes the 8-marker pool: earn the top card face-down and return all markers to the pool. The two remaining Fear move two markers toward the next card. Terror II applies immediately when its divider is exposed; the earned card is resolved during the Fear step in order, one at a time.

evidence.text: Fear is island-wide. For each Fear, move one marker from the Fear Pool to Generated Fear. When all **4 per Spirit** markers have moved, earn the top Fear Card face-down, return all markers to the pool and continue with any leftover Fear toward the next card. If earning a card exposes a Terror divider, the new Terror Level applies immediately; its victory condition can end the game at the outcome check. Earning the final card reveals Victory; its text never needs resolving.

2. **Fear:** Turn the earned face-down stack over and resolve its cards **in the order earned**, one at a time, without looking ahead. Use **only the current Terror Level's effect**, even if the card was earned at a lower level. Discard each resolved card to Fear discard. Fear earned during this step can earn more cards: append them to the bottom of the resolving stack and resolve them this same step. Subsequent cards use any newly reached Terror Level. Fear earned later, such as in Ravage or Slow, waits for the next Fear step.

answers.answer: Damage marks a piece and destroys it at Health; Destroy returns it regardless of Health and Town/City destruction gives Fear; Remove takes it off without a Health test or destruction Fear; Replace removes it and puts the new piece in its place retaining marked Damage, with Fear only if that retained Damage destroys the replacement. Damage from separate normal Powers can accumulate during a turn. Normal Spirit Damage does not harm Dahan.

evidence.text:
| Instruction | Effect on the piece |
| --- | --- |
| **Damage** | Mark Damage; reaching Health destroys the piece immediately. |
| **Destroy** | Return the specified piece to supply regardless of Health or marked Damage. |
| **Remove** | Take the specified piece off the board without a Damage-to-Health test. |
| **Replace** | Remove the original piece and put the specified new piece in its place, retaining marked Damage. |

“Damage” means **Damage to Invaders** unless explicitly stated otherwise. Normal Spirit Damage does not harm Dahan or the land. Distribute Damage among Invaders in the target land however you wish; Explorers need not be hit first. Damage from separate normal Powers and counterattacks can accumulate within a turn. A piece is destroyed immediately when its marked Damage reaches/exceeds its Health. Reduced Health can also destroy a previously damaged piece; Damage does not itself reduce Health. Marked Damage does not reduce the Health counted by a Health-worth removal allowance. If a damaged piece moves out of a Health bonus or into a Health penalty and is thereby destroyed, destruction occurs in its destination land, never in an in-between location. answers.answer: Separate Power uses cannot combine Bringer’s hypothetical Damage; 2 plus 1 in separate Powers does not destroy the City. Instructions within one Power can combine, and a Repeat can pretend-destroy the same piece again.

evidence.text:
- **Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares:** Its Powers' explicit Damage/Destroy cannot actually harm Invaders/Dahan or destroy anything except its own Presence. This restriction still applies when that Power's Damage/Destroy instruction names Dahan or another Spirit as the actor. An explicit instruction to Damage or Destroy Dahan does nothing to those Dahan; skip that instruction and resolve the rest of the Power normally. For each Power use, evaluate what it would destroy if resolved normally. Apply these results separately to each would-be-destroyed Invader; the Fear result does not itself grant movement:

  | Would-be-destroyed Invader | Fear | Movement from this special rule |
  | --- | --- | --- |
  | Explorer | 0 | Push it. |
  | Town | 2 | Push it. |
  | City | 5 | No Push. |

  No real Damage is marked, so different Powers or a Repeat cannot combine their hypothetical Damage; multiple instructions **within one Power** can. Existing real Damage from others helps its hypothetical destruction and remains unchanged afterward. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once. Repeats can “destroy” the same piece again for Fear. It does not get bonuses conditional on **actual** destruction (e.g., Mists of Oblivion or Vengeance of the Dead) from these pretend destructions. [Core: .7w4g9jv, .7w4g7yx, .7w4g7yu, .7w4g8pj, .9v5kfh3, .9v5katc, .bu6oc6g]

| Instruction | Effect on the piece |
| --- | --- |
| **Damage** | Mark Damage; reaching Health destroys the piece immediately. |
| **Destroy** | Return the specified piece to supply regardless of Health or marked Damage. |
| **Remove** | Take the specified piece off the board without a Damage-to-Health test. |

[FAQ if-an-invader-with-health-bonus-and-damage-is-moved-where-is-it-destroyed]

**Destroy** returns pieces to supply regardless of Health when directly instructed. Every destroyed Town generates **1 Fear** and every destroyed City **2 Fear**, in addition to explicit Fear from the effect. Explorers generate none automatically. **Remove** returns the specified pieces without requiring Damage to reach their Health and without destruction Fear. Within the effect's count and piece-type restrictions, its decision-maker may choose any eligible pieces; there is no Explorer-first priority unless stated. **Replace** removes a piece and adds another, retaining its marked Damage: the replacement itself produces no Fear, but if the retained Damage destroys the new piece, destruction Fear applies normally. For simultaneous replacements, select all pieces before replacing any: the same original City cannot become a Town and then an Explorer within that one simultaneous instruction. Separate completed instructions or actions may replace the resulting piece again (e.g., successive players resolving **Trade Suffers** at Terror III).
